questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is NOT in accordance with the property stated against it?
options: $HI > HBr > HCl > HF$ [Acidic Property in Water]
questions.solution:
The oxidising power of halogens decreases down the group: $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$.

The acidic strength of hydrogen halides in water increases down the group due to a decrease in bond dissociation enthalpy: $HI > HBr > HCl > HF$.

Electronegativity decreases down the group: $F > Cl > Br > I$.

The bond dissociation energy of halogens does not follow a regular trend. Due to strong interelectronic repulsions between the lone pairs on the small fluorine atoms, the $F-F$ bond is weaker than the $Cl-Cl$ and $Br-Br$ bonds. The correct order of bond dissociation energy is $Cl_2 > Br_2 > F_2 > I_2$.

Thus, the order $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$ for bond dissociation energy is incorrect.

Answer: $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$ [Bond Dissociation Energy]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Given are $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_2, \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_3, \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_4$ and $\mathrm{H}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_7$. Which of the above oxacids results into two series of salts?
questions.solution:
The number of series of salts formed by an oxoacid is equal to its basicity, which corresponds to the number of ionizable hydrogen atoms attached to oxygen atoms (P-OH groups).

For $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_2$ (hypophosphorous acid), the structure is $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{P(O)OH}$. It has only one P-OH group, so it is monobasic and forms one series of salts.

For $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_3$ (phosphorous acid), the structure is $\mathrm{HP(O)(OH)}_2$. It has two P-OH groups, so it is dibasic and forms two series of salts (acid salts and normal salts).

For $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4$ (phosphoric acid), the structure is $\mathrm{OP(OH)}_3$. It has three P-OH groups, so it is tribasic and forms three series of salts.

For $\mathrm{H}_4\mathrm{P}_2\mathrm{O}_7$ (pyrophosphoric acid), the structure is $\mathrm{(HO)}_2\mathrm{P(O)OP(O)(OH)}_2$. It has four P-OH groups, so it is tetrabasic and forms four series of salts.

Therefore, $\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_3$ results in two series of salts.

Answer: $\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following will not liberate nitrogen on reaction with nitrous acid?
questions.solution:
Nitrous acid (HNO_{2}$) reacts with primary aliphatic amines (R-NH_{2}$) to form unstable diazonium salts, which decompose to evolve nitrogen gas (N_{2}$) and form alcohols. Ethylamine (CH_{3}CH_{2}NH_{2}$), methylamine (CH_{3}NH_{2}$), and 2-aminopropane ($(CH_{3})_{2}CHNH_{2}$) are all primary aliphatic amines and will liberate nitrogen gas.

Dimethylamine ($(CH_{3})_{2}NH$) is a secondary aliphatic amine. Secondary amines react with nitrous acid to form N-nitrosamines, which are yellow oily compounds. The reaction is: $(CH_{3})_{2}NH + HNO_{2} \rightarrow (CH_{3})_{2}N-N=O + H_{2}O$. No nitrogen gas is evolved in this reaction.

Answer: dimethylamine$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the chemical reaction, $\mathrm{N}_{2}+3 \mathrm{H}_{2} \rightleftarrows 2 \mathrm{NH}_{3}$ at equilibrium point.
options: equal volumes of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ are reacting.
equal manes of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ are reacting.
the same amount of ammonia is formed, as it is decomposed into $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$.
questions.solution:
The chemical reaction $\mathrm{N}_{2} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2} \rightleftarrows 2\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ represents a reversible process at equilibrium.

At equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction (formation of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$) is equal to the rate of the backward reaction (decomposition of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ into $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$).

This implies that the amount of ammonia being formed per unit time is exactly equal to the amount of ammonia being decomposed per unit time, maintaining constant concentrations of all species involved.

Therefore, the condition at equilibrium is that the rate of formation of ammonia equals the rate of its decomposition.

Answer: the same amount of ammonia is formed, as it is decomposed into $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The decreasing order of stability of oxides of halogen is
questions.solution: In oxides of halogen, the bonds are mainly covalent due to small difference in electronegativity between the halogens and oxygen. The bond polarity, however, increases as we move from $F$ to $I$. The stability of oxides of iodine is greater than those of chlorine, while bromine oxides are the least stable. Iodine-oxygen bond is stable due to greater polarity of the bond, while the stability of the chlorine-oxygen bond is due to multiple bond formation involving $d$-orbitals of the chlorine atom. Bromine being in between lacks both these characteristics. Thus, the stability of oxides of halogens decreases in the following order $\mathrm{I}$>$\mathrm{Cl}$>$\mathrm{Br}$>$\mathrm{F}$
